scenarios.title: The Circular Track
scenarios.setup: A car on a circular test track. The odometer counts every metre driven (distance), a gold arrow always points from the start line to the car (displacement), a blue arrow shows the car's velocity and an orange one its acceleration.

law.name: Scalars and vectors
law.formula: vector = size + direction

concept.title: Scalars and vectors
concept.idea: A scalar has only a size (a number and a unit). A vector has a size and a direction, so it is drawn as an arrow. Two vectors add like arrows placed head to tail, not like plain numbers.
examples: Scalars: distance, speed, mass, time, temperature, energy, work, power
Vectors: displacement, velocity, acceleration, force, momentum, impulse, weight
3 m east + 4 m north is not 7 m: it is a 5 m arrow pointing north-east

trials.prompt: The car drives 3 m due east, turns left and drives 4 m due north. Its odometer will show 7 m. Predict the size of its displacement from the start.
trials.outcome: 5 m, pointing north-east, although the odometer reads 7 m.
trials.explanation: Distance only adds up the path: 3 + 4 = 7 m, a scalar. Displacement is the straight arrow from start to finish, a vector. The two legs are at right angles, so its size is √(3² + 4²) = 5 m, and it has a direction too.

law.name: Distance and displacement
law.formula: displacement = straight line from start to finish

concept.title: Distance and displacement
concept.idea: Distance is how much ground you cover, measured along the path: a scalar. Displacement is the change in position: an arrow from where you started to where you are now, a vector. Go round in a circle and they can be very different.
examples: A runner on a 400 m track runs 400 m but ends where she started
A taxi meter charges for distance, not displacement
A plane flying 300 km north then 400 km east has a displacement of 500 km north-east

trials.prompt: The track is a circle 100 m round (radius 15.9 m). The car drives half a lap from the start line. Predict the odometer (distance) and the length of the displacement arrow.
trials.outcome: Distance 50 m; displacement 31.8 m.
trials.explanation: Distance is the length of track driven: 0.5 × 100 = 50 m. Displacement is the straight chord from the start to the car: 2 × radius = 31.8 m. The straight line is always the shortest path, so displacement is never more than distance.

law.name: Speed and velocity
law.formula: speed = distance ÷ time; velocity = displacement ÷ time

concept.title: Speed and velocity
concept.idea: Speed is how fast the distance grows: a scalar. Velocity is how fast the displacement changes: speed in a stated direction, a vector. Two cars at 60 km/h going opposite ways have the same speed but different velocities.
examples: A speedometer shows speed, not velocity
Weather reports give wind velocity: 20 km/h from the west
A satellite in orbit has steady speed but its velocity is always changing direction

concept.title: Acceleration
concept.idea: Acceleration is how quickly velocity changes. Because velocity is a vector, you accelerate when you speed up, when you slow down (a negative acceleration, or deceleration) and when you change direction.

A car braking at a red light (negative acceleration)

Going round a roundabout at steady speed

scenarios.title: The Crash Lab
scenarios.setup: A low-friction air track with carts of different masses, a Newton's cradle, and a drop tower where an egg falls onto a concrete slab or a thick foam cushion. Live readouts show mass, velocity, momentum, force and impact time.

law.name: Conservation of momentum
law.formula: total momentum before = total momentum after

concept.title: Momentum
concept.idea: Momentum is mass in motion: how hard it is to stop something. It is mass × velocity, so it has a direction. In a collision with no outside force, the total momentum of everything involved stays the same: it is passed on, never lost.
examples: A slow lorry can have more momentum than a fast bicycle
A rifle recoils backwards as the bullet goes forwards
A Newton's cradle passes momentum through the balls
Rockets push gas backwards to gain forward momentum

trials.prompt: Cart A (1 kg) moves at 6 m/s to the right. Cart B (2 kg) is at rest. They collide and stick together. Predict their velocity just after (+ to the right, − to the left).
trials.outcome: 2 m/s to the right.
trials.explanation: Momentum p = m × v, with a sign for its direction. Before: 1 × 6 + 2 × 0 = 6 kg·m/s. No outside force acts, so the total is the same after: 6 ÷ 3 kg = 2 m/s.

law.name: Mass and weight

concept.title: Mass
concept.idea: Mass is the amount of matter in an object. It is a measure of inertia (how hard it is to change its motion), and it is the same everywhere in the universe. Weight is different: it is the force of gravity on that mass, so it changes from planet to planet.
examples: Measured with a beam balance by comparing with standard masses
1 kg is defined from the Planck constant; it used to be a platinum cylinder in Paris
